business_problem: G-bits needed a more flexible backend for a fast-growing mobile game because MySQL made sharding, scaling, failover, and schema changes for dynamic game attributes too slow and risky.
solution_summary: G-bits rebuilt the data layer for Yi Nian Xiao Yao on ApsaraDB for MongoDB, Alibaba Cloud's managed MongoDB service, so the studio could support rapid game changes and huge concurrency without manual database operations. Game state is stored as JSON documents, which lets developers add new weapons, props, and character attributes without the rigidity of relational schemas. The managed service expands and shrinks capacity for testing, launches, and live operations, while same-availability-zone deployment delivers roughly 400 microsecond average query response times for local players. High availability, retry and caching support, multi-threaded oplog recovery, backups, and workload isolation across nodes help the team keep gameplay uninterrupted while reducing the operations burden on the developers running the title.

solution_components.name: ApsaraDB for MongoDB
solution_components.role: Stores game data as JSON documents and provides elastic scaling, high availability, recovery, and workload isolation for the Yi Nian Xiao Yao backend.

data_flow: Game character, item, and operations data is written as JSON documents to ApsaraDB for MongoDB, game services query the same-availability-zone deployment for low-latency reads, and backup, oplog recovery, retry, and caching mechanisms keep sessions available during failures.
business_outcome: G-bits supported tens of millions of players with hundreds of thousands online concurrently, improved outage recovery 50x, at least doubled operational efficiency, and freed the team to focus on new game features and global expansion.
